--- title: "Unreported Detention: ICE Facilities in FY 2026" subtitle: "An analysis of ICE detention statistics not included in the February 2026 annual detention report" description: "Comparing the Deportation Data Project's daily detention counts with ICE's published FY 2026 annual statistics to identify unreported facilities and track population changes" author: "Carwil Bjork-James" date: last-modified format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-fold: true execute: echo: false warning: false message: false --- ## Overview This page analyzes ICE detention during the first months of fiscal year 2026, comparing two data sources: 1. **ICE FY 2026 annual detention statistics**, released February 12, 2026, with data through February 5, 2026. Published at the [ICE Detention Management Division](https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management), the spreadsheet covers 220 facilities. 2. **Deportation Data Project daily population data**, government data obtained by FOIA and [archived](https://deportationdata.org/data/processed/ice.html) by the [Deportation Data Project](https://deportationdata.org/). The dataset covers every ICE detention facility with reported daily counts from October 2022 through August 5, 2026. DDP's 20260806 release no longer publishes the daily-population file, so it is recreated here from DDP's detention-stints records following DDP's published methodology (validated to reproduce DDP's earlier published file exactly; see `R/ddp-daily-population.R`). Significantly, both of these are government-generated datasets, provided more and less willingly (respectively) by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Where doing comparisons below, we focus on the October 1, 2025 – February 12, 2026 period covered by the ICE FY 2026 spreadsheet. Where summarizing detention as a whole, and in drawing the sparkline graphs for each facility on the map, we go as far as the DDP allows. As with [FY 2025](../ddp-comparison/index.qmd), the DDP data reveals a substantial unreported detention population — facilities where ICE holds people that do not appear in the published annual statistics. Over this period, the unreported population reached a peak of over 2,500 individuals on a single day. Medical facilities, which accounted for about 68 detainees per day in FY 2025, have been excluded from this dataset. ::: {.callout-note} This analysis previously used DDP's 20260330 daily-population release (data through March 10, 2026). DDP retroactively revised some records in the 20260806 release, so the two data states differ slightly within the comparison window. The original through-March analysis is archived as `ddp-comparison-26-20260330.qmd`, with its data exports in `data/ddp-comparison-export-fy26-20260330/`. ::: In FY 2026, it is Hold Rooms and other Staging facilities that account for the vast majority of the unreported population. For comparison, hold facilties in FY 2025 had an average daily population of about 1,163 detainees, with an average of 1,986 in the final 60 days. Three facilities that appear in the February 12 ICE roster — Lewisburg US Penitentiary, the Guantánamo Migrant Operations Center, and Lafayette Parish Correctional Center — were originally unlinked to their DDP codes because ICE lists them under different names. Manual matches connect them here (canonical IDs 403, 404, and 402), so they do not appear in the unmatched analysis below. For the opposite problem — facilities that ICE itself removed from the FY26 roster after February — see the roster-churn table below. ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Aggregate comparison The ICE FY 2026 spreadsheet covers **October 1, 2025 through February 5, 2026** — 128 days. To compare with the DDP data we compute average daily population (ADP) over that same window. ::: {#tbl-aggregate .cell tbl-cap='Aggregate comparison: ICE FY26 annual stats vs. DDP daily average (Oct 1 2025 – Feb 5 2026)'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Source | Facilities| Total ADP| |:---------------------|----------:|---------:| |ICE FY26 annual stats | 220| 67139| |DDP daily average | 557| 69428| ::: ::: The DDP covers 557 facility codes with at least one detainee during this period, compared to 220 in the ICE spreadsheet. On average, 2,289 more detainees per day appear in the DDP data than in ICE's published figures. ### Daily population over time ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Total ICE detained population per day (DDP data, Jan 2025 – Aug 2026)](ddp-comparison-26_files/figure-html/fig-daily-total-1.png){#fig-daily-total width=672} ::: ::: ## Facility-level matching ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Category |Value | |:-----------------------------|:-----------| |In both sources |219 | |ICE only (no DDP match) |1 | |Matched: ICE total ADP |67125 | |Matched: DDP total ADP |67353 | |Matched: aggregate difference |228 (0.34%) | ::: ::: ### Facility-level agreement ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![FY26 ADP comparison by facility (log scale). Dashed line = perfect agreement.](ddp-comparison-26_files/figure-html/fig-scatter-1.png){#fig-scatter width=672} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-agreement-bands .cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Agreement band | Facilities| |:----------------------------------------|----------:| |Within 10% | 152| |Within 25% | 22| |Within 50% | 26| |>50% difference | 19| |Public-facing report shows greater value | 99| ::: ::: Among the 219 matched facilities with nonzero ADP in both sources, 152 agree within 10%. There are 99 facilities with a lower count in DDP than in the ICE spreadsheet. ::: {#tbl-ice-only .cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: ICE FY26 facilities with no DDP match | ID|Facility | ICE ADP| |---:|:--------------------|-------:| | 372|Victoria County Jail | 14| ::: ::: 1 ICE FY26 facilities have no matching DDP facility code. ## Unmatched facilities {#sec-unmatched} **337** of 557 DDP facility codes do not appear in the ICE FY 2026 annual statistics. These are facilities where ICE holds detainees but which are excluded from the published spreadsheet. ### By facility type Facility types are drawn from the Vera Institute's classification system. "Dedicated" facilities are purpose-built or contractually dedicated to ICE detention. "Non-Dedicated" are county jails and other facilities that also hold ICE detainees. "Hold/Staging" are short-term ERO processing rooms. "Federal" includes BOP prisons and USMS facilities. ::: {#tbl-unmatched-types .cell tbl-cap='DDP facilities not in ICE FY26, by facility type and ADP class'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Facility type |Peak class | Facilities| Period ADP| |:-------------|:----------|----------:|----------:| |Hold/Staging |Peak ≥ 2 | 157| 1840| |Federal |Peak ≥ 2 | 37| 181| |Non-Dedicated |Peak ≥ 2 | 48| 46| |Family/Youth |Peak ≥ 2 | 3| 4| |Non-Dedicated |Peak < 2 | 51| 2| |Family/Youth |Peak < 2 | 2| 1| |Federal |Peak < 2 | 17| 1| |Hold/Staging |Peak < 2 | 14| 1| |Dedicated |Peak < 2 | 5| 0| |Dedicated |Peak ≥ 2 | 2| 0| |Other/Unknown |Peak < 2 | 1| 0| ::: ::: The 337 unmatched facilities account for an average daily population of **2,075** over the October 2025 – February 5, 2026 period. 90 facilities never had more than one detainee at a time, collectively contributing 4.2 ADP. ### Daily population in unmatched facilities ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Daily detained population in facilities not in ICE FY26 annual statistics](ddp-comparison-26_files/figure-html/fig-daily-unmatched-1.png){#fig-daily-unmatched width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Average daily population in unmatched facilities, by month and type](ddp-comparison-26_files/figure-html/fig-monthly-by-type-1.png){#fig-monthly-by-type width=672} ::: ::: ### Facilities dropped from the ICE roster ICE revises the FY26 facility roster with each spreadsheet release. The July 2026 release — now the pipeline's FY26 source — removed facilities that were still listed in the February 12 roster on which this comparison is based.
